summary: Iter10 backend testing (Vision/Misi + OKR↔BSC link + Komitmen PDF). Added /app/backend/tests/test_iter10_vision_komitmen.py with 17 tests. 16 passed, 1 failed. Iter9 regression (28 tests) still 100% pass. One real bug found: PUT /api/strategy/okr/{id} with bsc_target_id=null does NOT unset the link (server filters None values before $set), which contradicts the spec requirement 'PUT /okr/{id} setting bsc_target_id=null → GET returns bsc_target: null'.

critical.issue: Cannot unset bsc_target_id by sending null. Handler builds update dict as `{k:v for k,v in payload.model_dump().items() if v is not None}` — so any field explicitly sent as null is dropped and Mongo $set never runs for it. Same pattern also affects other Optional fields on OKR (divisi_id, owner_id) and mirrors patterns in update_period/update_bsc/update_kpi/update_project. Fix requires distinguishing 'field not sent' from 'field sent as null' — e.g. use `payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` (with Pydantic v2 `model_fields_set`) and then keep null values, OR add explicit `$unset` handling.

action_items: Fix PUT /api/strategy/okr/{id} to allow unsetting bsc_target_id (and other Optional fields) via explicit null. Recommended: switch to `payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` so unsent fields stay untouched but null values are actually applied. Apply the same fix consistently to update_period/update_bsc/update_kpi/update_project/update_kr for parity.

Consider embedding a font-fallback if PDF logo path is unavailable — currently /assets/ruang_sanad_logo.png exists so PDF size ~ acceptable; test uses > 5KB floor (actual ~ tens of KB). Spec asks '>100KB with logo embedded' — verify manually if logo needs to be larger/high-res.

rca of the issue: Root cause: strategy.py update_okr line 347 (also update_bsc/update_period/update_kpi/update_project/update_kr): `update = {k: v for k, v in payload.model_dump().items() if v is not None}`. Pydantic v2 model_dump() returns ALL fields (default None for unset). The comprehension can't distinguish 'user sent null' from 'user omitted field' — both look like None. Reproduction: POST OKR with bsc_target_id=<some_id>; PUT /okr/{id} json={'bsc_target_id': null}; GET /okr → bsc_target_id still set. Mitigation: use `payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` so only client-sent keys go to $set; null then flows through correctly. For fields that should truly not be null (e.g. period_id nama), keep field-level validators.
